name: Correctly source-bound service principal (SNS) - a NEGATIVE control, not a confused-deputy exposure
note: IAM-1207 (boundary of suite-2 test 27). An SNS topic access policy grants the EventBridge service principal sns:Publish, but ANDs aws:SourceArn (ArnEquals) with aws:SourceAccount (StringEquals). That is the AWS-documented confused-deputy mitigation, so the RESOURCE-CONFUSED-DEPUTY finding must drop to an INFORMATIONAL negative control - NOT an exposure, NOT public write. It must not report a missing source binding and must not infer whether the referenced rule exists.
rationale: A service principal is NOT a public principal, so PUBLIC-ACCESS must never fire on events.amazonaws.com. The confused-deputy problem is that a resource policy trusting a service principal authorizes the SERVICE, not the actor who configured it; the AWS-documented fix is aws:SourceArn and/or aws:SourceAccount, which scope the service to act only on behalf of a specific source. Here BOTH are present and ANDed (ArnEquals aws:SourceArn + StringEquals aws:SourceAccount), so the grant is a correctly source-bound relationship - an informational NEGATIVE control, not an exposure. The analyzer must not warn about a missing source binding and must not infer whether the referenced EventBridge rule actually exists. Effective access still depends on identity policies and other layers not supplied. Ref: docs/resource-policy-semantics.md sec 4; confused-deputy (aws:SourceArn / aws:SourceAccount).
